data.name: CaptureTitle
data.value: 2. Opt-in capture

data.name: CaptureHelp
data.value: The hooks can send your agent sessions to Athar, which suggests memories from them. Nothing is captured unless you list the repository.

data.name: CaptureOptIn
data.value: Capture runs only for the repositories you choose on My sessions, for all your machines at once. Pause there stops everything.

data.name: CaptureSent
data.value: A captured session sends its transcript when it ends or compacts. Pending batches wait in ~/.athar/outbox until they're sent.

data.name: CaptureRedacted
data.value: Secrets such as passwords and keys are redacted on your machine and again on the server.

data.name: CaptureReview
data.value: Athar extracts suggested memories into your inbox. Nothing becomes a team or company memory without review.

data.name: CaptureStop
data.value: To stop one repository, remove it on My sessions, or list it in capture_exclude on a machine. Revoking the token stops that machine.

data.name: VsCodeHelp
data.value: GitHub Copilot in agent mode uses Athar's tools. VS Code signs in with your Athar account and doesn't capture sessions.

data.name: VsStepMcp
data.value: Add the server to your user mcp.json (Command Palette › MCP: Open User Configuration). VS Code opens the browser to sign in the first time you start it.

data.value: Optional: save the skill in a repository so Copilot knows when to use Athar.

data.name: VsStepCheck
data.value: Open Copilot Chat in Agent mode, start the athar server from the tools list and ask something your wiki answers.

data.name: QuickTitle
data.value: Quick setup

data.name: QuickHelp
data.value: One command sets up every agent it finds on this computer: the Claude Code plugin (skill, capture hooks, Athar over OAuth), Codex (Athar, the skill and the hooks) and VS Code. It asks for your access token without showing it, and saves it only in ~/.athar/config.json for the capture hooks. Needs Node 22.15 or later.

data.name: QuickAfter
data.value: Then sign in once in each agent: /mcp in Claude Code, codex mcp login athar for Codex, and the athar server in VS Code. The tabs below do the same by hand.

data.value: Sign in to Athar in the browser:

data.name: VsStepPat
data.value: No browser on that machine? Use an access token instead. VS Code asks for it once and keeps it in its secret storage, not in the file.

data.name: OpenSessions
data.value: Choose repositories on My sessions

data.name: QuickIngest
data.value: Then, to add a folder of documents to a project: athar ingest <folder> --project <project id>. It sends Markdown, text and HTML files (skipping what .gitignore ignores), and later runs send only what changed.
